title: System Design Starter: From One Computer to Many

sections.heading: Everyday analogy
sections.body:
Think of a food court. One stall is one server. When lunch rush hits, you add stalls, split jobs, and need a way to find the right stall.

Distributed system means many computers working as one team. Service discovery is the directory board that tells you where each stall is. Consistent hashing is the rule for which stall handles which customer, so adding a stall moves only a few customers.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body:
One computer hits limits on traffic, storage, and failures. System design spreads work so the service stays fast and available.

Idempotent API means doing the same request twice gives the same result, like pressing pay again does not charge twice. This is needed because networks retry. JWT authentication is a signed pass that proves who you are without asking a central desk every time.

sections.heading: What can go wrong
sections.body:
More machines means more ways to fail. If service discovery is stale, requests go to dead servers. If hashing is uneven, one server gets overloaded.

Without idempotent APIs, retries create duplicate orders. Bloom filter is a fast maybe-check to avoid expensive lookups, but it can say maybe when answer is no, so you still need a real check.

steps.narration: Client sends a request like place order.
Consistent hashing picks which server owns this key.
Server handles it; JWT proves identity.
If network fails, retry is safe because API is idempotent.

quiz.q: What does an idempotent API guarantee?
options: Same request twice has same effect as once
Server stores all past requests forever
quiz.why: Idempotent means retries do not create duplicates, key for unreliable networks.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x without consistent hashing?
options: One server gets overloaded while others sit idle
quiz.why: Poor distribution causes hot spots; consistent hashing limits reshuffling and balances load.

options: To locate healthy service instances dynamically
quiz.why: Servers come and go; discovery keeps the directory current.

extra: Bloom filters have false positives but never false negatives.
